boundary_evidence: Overlay 0 is one function and its data: .text 0x020aa420..0x020aa4c8 holds InitializeAssetHandleTable alone, and .data 0x020aa4e0..0x020bf4e0 holds 2058 NUL-terminated asset path strings followed by the 2058-entry pointer table at 0x020bd4b8 that the function indexes by handle. The overlay has no .rodata, .bss or .ctor contents, so the whole module is this one source.

The strings are not in table order: they are sorted shortest first, each padded to 4 bytes. That is how mwccarm 2004/b56 lays out the string literals of a C initializer, one .data section per literal, so a single array of literal paths in table order reproduces both the strings and the table byte for byte, including the order of equal-length strings.

Every one of the table's 2058 words is a relocation to one of those strings, and nothing outside the overlay refers to the strings or the table: ov000 is resident only inside func_0201a2f8 (tools/overlay_residency.py, rule E1), so references from other modules that dsd recorded as overlays(0,...) were never ov000's and now name their remaining candidates.
notes: The path strings are native string literals; their @NNN names are compiler-numbered, so editing the initializer (adding or removing a literal) renumbers them and this manifest's data and relocation rows with them.
